17D.15 We should not believe in our own righteousness.

precepts.text: The Most High held Moses by him a long season on Sinai, shewed him the secrets of the times and the end, and commanded which words to declare and which to hide.
precepts.point: What was he doing those forty days? He was receiving the understanding of the beginning of times, the midst of times, and the end of times; that is why some things Moses wrote, like Genesis 49 and Deuteronomy 32 and 33, are hard to understand, hidden in plain view, while keep the commandments is written easy.
precepts.why:
What was Moses doing those forty days and forty nights in the mount, neither eating bread nor drinking water? Esdras is told: “In the bush I did manifestly reveal myself unto Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt: And I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to the mount of where I held him by me a long season, And told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end; and commanded him, saying, These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.”

He was receiving the understanding of the beginning of times, the midst of times and the end of times. That is why some things Moses wrote, like Genesis 49 and Deuteronomy 32 and 33, are hard to understand, hidden in plain view, while keep the commandments is written easy: the Most High commanded him which words to declare and which to hide.

precepts.text: There is no fear of God before their eyes; religion removed the fear and austerity of the Most High from before us, and this is the result.
precepts.point: Religion has tried to remove the fierceness, the wrath, and the severity of the Most High and push an effeminate white Jesus in front of us that loves everybody, forgives everything at the last breath with no commandments kept, and can do no wrong. We are suffering in all our cities, in Africa, in Europe, and in the Caribbean from that lack of fear of God before our eyes.
precepts.why:
“There is no fear of God before their eyes.” Religion removed the fear and austerity of the Most High from before us, and this is the result.

Look at the Most High here: “Let me alone, that I may destroy them, and blot out their name from under heaven: and I will make of thee a nation mightier and greater than they.” He was ready to go back to the days of the flood and start over with one man; time means nothing to the Ancient of days. That is the fierceness, the wrath and the severity of the Most High.

Religion has tried to remove all of that and push an effeminate white Jesus in front of us that loves everybody, forgives everything at the last breath with no commandments kept, and can do no wrong. We are suffering in all our cities, in Africa, in Europe and in the Caribbean from that lack of fear of God before our eyes.

precepts.text: Esdras prayed the same prayer as Moses for Israel, and the Most High answered that the sinners are reserved to the end while he rejoices over the disposition of the righteous.
precepts.point: Esdras prayed the same prayer as Moses for the children of Israel, so precept these two prayers together: pay no attention to the fakers, for they remove themselves, but be merciful to us who have no works of righteousness, for by that mercy thou shalt be called merciful. When we are in the midst of sin we live worse than beasts, for a beast runs on instinct, but we consciously choose to go against the laws of the Most High.
precepts.why:
Esdras prayed the same prayer as Moses for the children of Israel, so precept these two prayers together. Moses: “destroy not thy people and thine inheritance, which thou hast redeemed through thy greatness”; “look not unto the stubbornness of this people, nor to their wickedness, nor to their sin”. Esdras: “O look not upon the sins of thy people; but on them which serve thee in truth.”

Pay no attention to the fakers, for they remove themselves: “Think not upon those that have walked feignedly before thee: but remember them, which according to thy will have known thy fear.” And be merciful to us who have no works of righteousness, for by that mercy thou shalt be called merciful: “For if thou hast a desire to have mercy upon us, thou shalt be called merciful, to us namely, that have no works of righteousness.”

“Let it not be thy will to destroy them which have lived like beasts”. When we are in the midst of sin we live worse than beasts, for a beast runs on instinct, but we consciously choose to go against the laws of the Most High.

The Most High answered: “Some things hast thou spoken aright, and according unto thy words it shall be. For indeed I will not think on the disposition of them which have sinned before death, before judgment, before destruction: But I will rejoice over the disposition of the righteous, and I will remember also their pilgrimage, and the salvation, and the reward, that they shall have.” The sinners are reserved to the end, while he rejoices over the disposition of the righteous.

points: Hear, O Israel: thou art to pass over Jordan this day, to possess nations greater and mightier than thyself, a people great and tall, the children of the Anakims, of whom it was said, who can stand before the children of Anak.
The Lord thy God goeth over before thee as a consuming fire; he shall destroy them and bring them down before thy face, so shalt thou drive them out and destroy them quickly.

Speak not thou in thine heart, saying, for my righteousness the Lord hath brought me in to possess this land: here is more of the Christianity spirit corrected. Israel entered for the wickedness of those nations and to perform the word sworn unto Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, not for their own uprightness.

Understand that the only reason any of us have a roof over our head and food in our stomach right now is the mercy and righteousness of the Most High, for thou art a stiffnecked people; it is because of him that we survive every single day.
Remember, and forget not, how thou provokedst the Lord thy God to wrath in the wilderness: from the day of leaving Egypt unto this place, ye have been rebellious against the Lord.
Moses abode in the mount forty days and forty nights, neither eating bread nor drinking water, when he went up to receive the tables of the covenant.

What was he doing those forty days? He was receiving the understanding of the beginning of times, the midst of times, and the end of times; that is why some things Moses wrote, like Genesis 49 and Deuteronomy 32 and 33, are hard to understand, hidden in plain view, while keep the commandments is written easy.

The Lord delivered unto me two tables of stone written with the finger of God: God took his time and wrote the ten commandments down himself, according to all the words which the Lord spake with you in the mount out of the midst of the fire.
Arise, get thee down quickly; thy people have corrupted themselves and made them a molten image. That molten image was the calf, the Egyptian goddess Hathor; you can look that up yourself.

Let me alone, that I may destroy them, and blot out their name from under heaven, and I will make of thee a nation mightier and greater than they. The Most High was ready to go back to the days of the flood and start over with one man; time means nothing to the Ancient of days.
Moses came down from the mount, the mount burning with fire, the two tables of the covenant in his two hands, and behold, ye had sinned against the Lord your God and made you a molten calf.

Ye had turned aside quickly out of the way which the Lord had commanded you: the Most High had been proving them through hard times, and they quickly turned back, just as many today go right back to their old ways the moment they are left alone. Brothers and sisters, check yourselves; we must endure to the end and rehearse the righteous acts now.
Moses took the two tables, cast them out of his two hands, and brake them before your eyes.

Moses fell down before the Lord, as at the first, forty days and forty nights, neither eating bread nor drinking water, because of all your sins; that is two forty-day fasts, for he was afraid of the anger and hot displeasure wherewith the Lord was wroth against the people.

The Lord was very angry with Aaron to have destroyed him, and Moses prayed for Aaron also at the same time. Moses prayed, and the Lord hearkened unto him; there arose no prophet like Moses, a mighty great man in the scriptures.
He took your sin, the calf which ye had made, burnt it with fire, stamped it, ground it very small until it was as small as dust, and cast the dust into the brook that descended out of the mount.
At Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibrothhattaavah ye provoked the Lord to wrath, and at Kadeshbarnea ye rebelled against the commandment of the Lord and believed him not.
Ye have been rebellious against the Lord from the day that I knew you: Moses called Israel out plainly, and it is real talk still.

Moses fell down before the Lord forty days and forty nights because the Lord had said he would destroy the people, and prayed: O Lord God, destroy not thy people and thine inheritance, which thou hast redeemed through thy greatness.

Remember thy servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; look not unto the stubbornness of this people, nor to their wickedness, lest the land whence thou broughtest us out say the Lord was not able to bring them in, and because he hated them he brought them out to slay them.
